heroText: Ankara works best as a base in Turkey when you anchor days around Anitkabir, Museum of Anatolian Civilizations and Ankara Castle. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Esenboğa International Airport (ESB) handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.label: 1000 BC
history.text: The city grew significantly in size and importance under the Phrygians starting around 1000 BC, and experienced a large expansion following the mass migration from Gordion, (the capital of Phrygia), after an earthquake which severely damaged that city around that time.
The town was reincorporated into the Roman Empire under Emperor Aurelian in 272.

history.label: 5th century
history.text: After Constantinople became the East Roman capital, emperors in the 4th and 5th centuries would retire from the humid summer weather on the Bosporus to the drier mountain atmosphere of Ancyra.

In 654, the city, also known in Arabic sources as Qalat as-Salasil ("fortress of the chains"), was captured for the first time by the Arabs of the Rashidun Caliphate, under Muawiyah, the future founder of the Umayyad Caliphate.
Following its annexation by the Seljuk Turks in 1073, the city became known in many European languages as Angora; it was also known in Ottoman Turkish as Engürü (انگورو).
Ankara has experienced a phenomenal growth since it was made Turkey's capital in 1923, when it was "a small town of no importance".
